references.text: The taskmasters (נֹגְשִׂים) are mentioned for the first time here, where they were placed over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor.
God had seen the oppression by the taskmasters (נֹגְשִׂים), the same ones who now carry out Pharaoh's orders.
Pharaoh gave orders to the taskmasters and overseers on that day to stop providing straw, which is now being withheld from the people.
The officers (שֹׁטְרִים) of the Israelites were beaten because the people could not produce as many bricks.
Moses and Aaron had just been with Pharaoh, and his reply 'Thus says Pharaoh' (כֹּה אָמַר פַּרְעֹה) stands in contrast to 'Thus says the Lord'.
Isaiah uses the same word for oppressors (נֹגְשִׂים) when he describes Israel's suffering under tyrants.
In the messianic future, the taskmasters (נֹגְשִׂים) will be replaced by justice, in contrast to the oppression in Egypt.
The increasing oppression in the source verse is the concrete unfolding of Pharaoh's refusal, which leads to the great judgments described in 7:4.
